title: Oven Fish & Chips
subtitle: crunchy panko-crusted haddock and thick-cut oven chips, with a quick lemon tartar sauce
imageAlt: Golden crumbed fish fillets and thick chips with lemon and tartar sauce on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Thaw the fish overnight in the fridge, then pat it very dry.
Oven at 230°C (450°F). The chips go in first; the fish needs only 12–15 minutes.

items.name: russet potatoes
items.note: about 4, cut in 1.5 cm thick chips

items.name: lemons
items.note: zest finely grated, then cut in wedges

steps.title: Chips in
steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F). Soak the chips in hot tap water 10 minutes, drain and pat very dry. Toss with the oil and salt and spread on a large parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet. Bake 35–40 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Toast the crumbs
steps.text: Toss the panko with the oil, paprika and garlic powder in a skillet over medium 3–4 minutes, stirring, until light golden. Tip into a shallow dish.

steps.title: Crumb the fish
steps.text: Pat the fish dry and season with the salt and pepper. Dip each piece in flour, then egg, then the toasted panko, pressing it on. Lay on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

steps.title: Bake the fish
steps.text: With 15 minutes left on the chips, bake the fish on the rack above 12–15 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 70°C (158°F) in the thickest piece.

steps.title: Tartar sauce
steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, chopped pickles and 1 tsp of the lemon zest together; cut the lemon in wedges.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the fish and chips with the tartar sauce and lemon wedges, and salt the chips while hot.

fixIt.fix: Toast the panko in the skillet first; it doesn't brown much in the oven on its own.
Bake it on a rack set over the baking sheet, or turn the pieces once.
Use parchment and dry the chips well before oiling.

saleTip: Frozen haddock or cod fillets at No Frills are much cheaper than fresh and taste just as good crumbed.
swap: Cod fillets: same amount and method.
leftovers: Best fresh; re-crisp leftovers in the air fryer.
doneness: Fish 70°C (158°F) in the thickest part and flakes easily with a fork (Health Canada, fish).
source: Based on tested oven-baked fish and chips methods (America's Test Kitchen, Canadian Living): pre-toasted panko crumb on haddock baked at 230°C, with soaked, oven-roasted thick chips.
prepAhead: Make the tartar sauce up to 2 days ahead.
Cut the chips and keep them in cold water in the fridge up to 1 day.
reheat: Air fryer at 190°C (375°F) 5–6 minutes or oven at 200°C (400°F) 8–10 minutes, until 74°C (165°F) and crisp.

basic.note: Salt-and-pepper crumb and plain chips with lemon; ketchup instead of tartar.

stepNotes.4: Basic: skip the tartar sauce; cut the lemon in wedges and serve with ketchup.

fancy.note: Mushy peas, the British chippy way.

addSteps.title: Mushy peas
addSteps.text: Simmer the peas in a little water 4 minutes, drain, then mash roughly with the butter and salt.

plating: Chips in a pile, fish leaning on them.
Tartar and mushy peas in small bowls.
Lemon wedges and a shake of salt.

why.1-5: Toasting the panko first gives a deep-fried colour and crunch without a pot of oil.
why.0-0: Thick-cut russets get a fluffy middle and crisp edges in a hot oven.
why.2-1: Sweet pickles give tartar sauce its tang and crunch.

funFact: Britain's fish and chips date to the 1860s; during WWII they were one of the few foods never rationed.
